claim_scope: conditional redesign-first governance responsibility for a knowingly accepted optional-disclosure procedure that foreseeably reveals a legitimate confidential exception

findings.claim: Privacy can concern facts inferred from public information or group data.
findings.evidence: Rumbold-Wilson and Loi-Christen excerpts already discuss inferential privacy or privacy rights over such inferences.

findings.claim: Predictable compliance can make an opt-out signal an exception.
findings.evidence: The assigned excerpts do not discuss the exact response-pattern case; search was bounded and does not prove absence.

findings.claim: A governance role creates a special obligation to repair the practice, possibly by cover refusal.
findings.evidence: Hart and Rawls provide adjacent practice/reciprocity ideas but do not establish this conclusion in the read passages; Hardimon primary text was unavailable; Singer gives a general-aid rival.

coverage_limitations: Only the exact excerpts and metadata in the sealed sources-001 packet were used.
No new literature search was authorized for this stage.
Hardimon, Role Obligations, was metadata only.
Hart was a single search-indexed p.185 excerpt; direct PDF extraction failed.
No broad claim that no prior work makes this argument is warranted.
permitted_conclusion: The bounded record did not locate an exact precedent, but neither the special-duty contribution nor its originality is established.
